newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius firm poised to invest in Ivorian sugar.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius firm poised to invest in Ivorian sugar.

text.p: Mauritian sugar firm Harel Freres Ltd is poised to take a stake in Ivory Coast's sugar industry as part of a consortium led by Ivorian group SIFCA, Harel Freres chairman said on Tuesday.

Cyril Mayer told Reuters that the consortium led by the Ivorian commodities leader emerged as "successful bidder" on one of two slices of Ivorian sugar parastatal SODESUCRE offered for sale by the government as part of its privatisation programme.
"This operation will allow us to export our know how and our expertise," Mayer told Reuters.
SODESUCRE, which has four sugar factories up for sale in two factory lots, is the latest government holding to be sold off in the West African nation under a wider privatisation programme.
SIFCA officials told Reuters on Tuesday in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's commercial capital, that its consortium had been named as "adjudicataire provisoire," or provisional purchaser.
Final purchase negotiations were still under way and no final decision had been announced by Ivory Coast, one said. Details would be available after the announcement although a date had not been set.
The SIFCA consortium bid for lot B -- the Borotou and Zuenoula sugar complexes together with a 99-year term lease on about 10,800 hectares of sugar cane plantations.
Mayer said Harel Freres representatives had arrived in Abidjan to finalise the deal.

"On the satisfactory conclusion of such negotiations, it is intended that the agricultural and industrial assets and related facilities of Borotou and Zuenoula sugar complexes will be sold by SODESUCRE to a company that will hold 55 percent with the remaining 45 percent held by the Ivorian government," he said.
Harel Freres, which is listed on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius, said it was the first time that a Mauritian sugar company had won a bid for sugar firms abroad against international competitors.
Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa producer, and the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius on the other side of Africa share a reputation for stability.
SIFCA, part of French-Ivorian group SIFCOM, trades in cocoa, coffee and rice and has also bid for many other Ivorian state firms recently up for privatisation from telecommunications to palm oil.
